question: Which Montgomery census tracts have the highest adult diabetes prevalence?

answer.sql: SELECT t.name AS tract_name, m.diabetes_crudeprev AS adult_diabetes_prevalence_percentage, m.totalpop18plus AS total_adult_population, t.geoid AS geoid FROM fw_pg.tracts t LEFT JOIN session.fw_af0a23_m1_cdc m ON m.tractfips = t.geoid ORDER BY CAST(m.diabetes_crudeprev AS DOUBLE) DESC, t.name ASC LIMIT 200

reasons: Rates answer the question: adult diabetes prevalence is a percentage per adult population (denominator adults/totalpop18plus), so ranking tracts by the rate is correct and no cross-series association is needed.
ORDER BY now casts the text prevalence to numeric DESC, fixing the prior lexicographic misranking; the preview shows correct descending order (31.5, 28.5, 28.2, ...).
The measure value precedes supporting columns, the 71-record Montgomery paired set is retained, and NULL prevalence tracts are excluded at the source so none remain to sort last.

points: Census Tract 24 leads with 31.5% adult diabetes prevalence (1,398 adults).
Tract 6 follows at 28.5% (1,203 adults), and Tract 7 at 28.2% (790 adults).
Tract 53.01 has the lowest prevalence at 3.9% (830 adults).
The gap between highest and lowest is 27.6 percentage points.
caveats: PLACES values are model-based estimates from survey data, not direct counts of diagnosed cases.
Rankings reflect the estimated prevalence percentage per adult population; absolute case counts are not provided.
Ties are resolved by the dataset's tie_groups; adjacent rows with equal values share a rank.
